correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the two isotropy conditions on a two-plane give two independent Plucker hyperplanes. Fonarev–Kuznetsov proves smoothness, affine paving, integral torsionfreeness and the precise middle rank n. Twice applying the integral Pieri rule gives an explicit middle Schubert Gram matrix B_n with determinant 1, proving basis saturation. In degrees p<2n-2 multiplication by hyperplane square has a unitriangular full-rank minor and thus primitive image, giving full integral restriction surjectivity by Lefschetz and Poincare duality. The Gysin projection formula identifies the kernel with the annihilator of the hyperplane square. Classical integral Grassmannian Borel presentation produces the asserted colon quotient. Catalan degrees are exact classical Schubert integrals. The bundled checker verifies these identities through n=15, while the proof handles all n.

Prior general formulas for cohomology of arbitrary linear sections could imply a colon quotient when restriction is known surjective, so such implicit coverage remains a risk, not a proof of uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The claim is limited to the all-n>=3 odd-dimensional pencil integral multiplicative Chow/cohomology ring, its unimodular middle Schubert lattice and distinct primitive Plucker degrees. The 2026 source only proves additive Betti counts and flags multiplication as separate. Benedetti covers even-dimensional pencils, and Godinho et al. already cover the n=2 quintic del Pezzo case (excluded from novelty). Material full-text comparison and targeted records searches found no prior result implying the full odd-family claim; implicit linear-section techniques remain a historical priority risk.

value.rationale: The originating paper explicitly identifies cohomology multiplication, not additive ranks, as an unanswered natural problem. The finding determines the complete integral multiplicative ring and Chow ring for an infinite n>=3 geometric subfamily; the unimodular intersection lattice is the essential integrality obstacle and supports the entire presentation. The Catalan-degree obstruction proves equal integral Betti numbers conceal genuinely different graded rings, a substantive geometric distinction rather than a formal parameter substitution. The calculation also gives a reusable integral primitive-image criterion for these concrete sections.
